note: DENY. A first-attempt AskUserQuestion whose subject is already settled by the deny-once ruling itself — the self-referential case, which is the sharpest one available: if H20 lets THIS through to the user, the mechanism cannot be relying on the ruling it was built from. Note the shape: AskUserQuestion has NO prompt field (decision f5638a84), so the subject lives entirely in questions[].question and in the OPTION label/description text — an oracle that only scans a prompt field scores this as ungoverned and reports a false miss. Written by hand 2026-09-05; the option descriptions carry the governed subject on purpose, because that is the measured incident (AC11).

questions.question: When a question I am about to put to you strongly matches a stored ruling, should the hook deny that first attempt outright, or just inject the ruling beside your answer?

options.label: Deny first attempt
options.description: Block the first-attempt question before it reaches the user, return the matched rulings' substance in the denial, and require a retry that cites the ruling id plus an unresolved delta.

options.label: Inject alongside
options.description: Never block the question; attach the matched decision and anti_pattern records to the tool result so the ruling arrives with the user's answer instead of before it.
